feature:connectors.title: Connected applications (Google, Slack, GitHub, MCP)
feature:connectors.purpose: Let owner-selected bots read from and act on external accounts through a fixed action catalog, with exact owner review or scoped standing permission for every mutation, durable receipts and owner reconciliation of uncertain effects. Credentials never reach bots.
logic: Owner creates a connection (provider, bots, actions, per-action resource allow-list) and connects it via OAuth (Google/GitHub with PKCE; Slack OAuth only over HTTPS) or a private token; MCP uses a public HTTPS endpoint plus discovery
Bots discover allowed actions with hermbot_connectors (connections.accessible) and call hermbot_connector -> /internal/tools -> service.tool_action -> connections.invoke
invoke authorizes bot/action, resolves remembered references, validates arguments against the fixed catalog and resource policy
Reads execute immediately using a refreshed credential; results are redacted, references remembered, Drive imports saved to the library; auth failures mark needs_reconnect

Mutations: one unfinished per task; outcome bound; frozen payload; queued directly when an owner requested authorization or a standing permission matches, else an exact owner review (approval + pending operation)
Owner Allow once queues the op (connection revision recheck); deny settles outcome and resumes bot; edit supersedes the op and creates a new review

Task worker drive_one rechecks grant, policy, task state, revision, payload hash, approval/authorization/standing budget, commits dispatching marker, calls provider, records receipt and resumes the bot
Lost receipts (stale dispatching lease) become uncertain; owner reconciles with evidence; unresolved closure only after task stopped
Revocation: best-effort provider revoke, local credential removal, standing permissions revoked, event sources paused

Connections tab: cards per connection (provider, status, account, assigned teammates, action count, error); Edit access, Connect/Reconnect (OAuth redirect), Use access token, Discover MCP tools, Revoke.
Add/Edit connection: provider google/slack/github/mcp (MCP needs HTTPS endpoint), teammates, permitted actions (mutation actions marked 'reviewed change'), per-action resource allow lists.
OAuth setup tab: client id/secret per provider and displayed callback URL.
Permissions tab: standing permission for one bot + action + exact resource with expiry hours and max uses; revoke.
Activity tab: operations with exact arguments/result receipt; uncertain/unresolved can be reconciled with provider evidence.
decisions: Fixed catalog of actions with server-side endpoints
Commit dispatching marker before the provider call; never auto-replay
All MCP tool calls treated as mutations
Connections never restrict native tools
Pinned-address transport with no redirects/proxies and bounded size/time
Embed operation identity in provider requests (Gmail Message-ID, Calendar id, Drive appProperties, Slack client_msg_id)

Connect once, enable for selected bots: OAuth lifecycle with encrypted credentials, refresh, revoke and reconnect kept in the backend; agents get scoped tool access only; Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack, GitHub and configurable MCP connections; prefer connectors over browser clicking.

Common authorization service for all connector mutations: approval covers the specific proposed action, editing invalidates stale approval, standing permissions are scoped and revocable, delegation never grants the recipient the sender's credentials, and terminal/browser paths cannot silently bypass connector policy.
Prefer a structured connector over clicking a website; connectors are installed account-wide via a marketplace of plugins
Milestone connectors chosen by the user: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack, GitHub plus extensible MCP and browser access

feature:routines.title: Routines (scheduled saved work)
feature:routines.purpose: Owner saves instructions, required results, inputs and a schedule; each occurrence becomes ordinary durable work with bounded overlap/missed/daily policies, history and explicit pause/resume/archive; chat can prepare inactive drafts.
logic: Save creates immutable revision + owner source message; state draft/active/paused; next_run_at computed by next_at
ensure_binding creates per-bot routine_schedulers token/generation; worker reconcile_schedulers pushes it to the runtime which creates a Hermes no-agent cron job
Every minute docker/routine_wakeup.py posts to /internal/routine-wake; wake authenticates and ticks
tick handles definite-failure pause, archived destination pause, missed occurrences (gap row, catch-up latest), admission and next_run_at/finished
admit dedupes occurrence, checks overlap/start window/daily cap/access, records skipped or admitted with frozen context (+since_success window) and creates the task via create_saved_task
Worker first claim locks the definition and rechecks start_allowed
Owner controls: Run now, pause, pause-stop, resume, archive; edits cancel unstarted queued runs
Entry: sidebar Routines or composer clock button (pre-fills instructions from draft; disabled with attachments, threads, coordination or no provider).

Editor: name, results conversation + teammate, optional team coordination grant, instructions, schedule kind once/interval/daily/weekdays/weekly/monthly with timezone, expected results (report/artifact/connector_effect/execution_check/native_effect), inputs, budget, start window, catch-up skip/latest, max runs per UTC day, information window since_success.
Live 'Next occurrences' preview via POST /routines/preview (350ms debounce); save blocked on preview error or no next occurrence when enabled.
List shows state, schedule text, next run, last run, errors and scheduler staleness (>180s); actions Edit, History, Run now, Pause/Resume, Pause and stop current run, Delete (archive, confirm).
History lists runs with status/origin/revision/output; Open run and results navigates to the conversation thread; Stop current run.
decisions: Use a Hermes native no-agent cron job only as a wake signal; DB decides due work
Missed runs skipped by default, optional latest within window, no backlog replay
One unfinished occurrence at a time (incl. unresolved connector effects/uncertain outcomes)
Three consecutive definite failures pause scheduling

Routines reuse Hermes scheduled jobs (no competing scheduler), with natural-language proposals plus editable schedule form, timezone-aware next-run preview, pause/resume, run now, history, and defined overlap, missed-run and failure behavior; unattended collaboration uses the same delegation tools and preserves initiating-user authorization.

Recurring orchestration: schedule a manager to coordinate specified bots with standing grants, budgets and initiating-user context; revocation prevents new dispatch and cancels owned pending work per the user's chosen stop action.
Routines are standing responsibilities attached to a bot, triggered by schedule or events (issues, PRs, webhooks, Slack, Linear), shown in the bot's main interface
Routines implemented as namespaced cron jobs [bot:<name>] whose runs land in the bot's chat history
Scheduler ticks every 60s with a file lock; jobs may load skills and run in a workdir
Hermes cron is only a wake signal: one supported --no-agent one-minute script job per active bot sends a scoped token; the database decides due occurrences and admits ordinary work.

feature:events.title: Event triggers (poll, Slack Socket Mode, signed webhooks)
feature:events.purpose: Owner-saved triggers start ordinary teammate work from authenticated provider events, with durable delivery/event/match/run records, own-write suppression, coalescing and bounded admission.
logic: Owner creates a source (provider, connection, transport, resource), saves secrets, and triggers with filters and saved instructions
event-worker claims sources with fenced leases; polls (Drive/Calendar/Gmail/GitHub) or runs Slack Socket Mode; http sources are verified then heartbeat
Webhook ingress verifies signatures and identity, then receive() -> ingest() commits before ack
ingest dedupes delivery and event identity, applies own-write suppression and per-trigger match/baseline/access, creates pending runs or coalesces
admit_pending converts ready runs into tasks through routines.create_saved_task (origin event)
Worker first-claim gate claim_locks/start_allowed
Lifecycle cascades: connection change, source edit/secrets/pause, conversation archive/membership pause triggers
Routines panel 'Events' mode hosts EventTriggers with views triggers, sources, edit, source-edit, history, deliveries.

Sources: Slack (Socket Mode app token), GitHub (poll or signed webhook), Google Drive/Calendar/Gmail (poll), generic signed webhook (Standard Webhooks headers); credential saved via /secrets with optional previous-key overlap; actions check/pause/archive/resync.

Trigger editor: source, event types, AND conditions (equals/contains/starts_with on provider-specific fields), teammate/conversation, coordination, instructions, expected results with optional 'request this action for every occurrence', limits (budget, start delay, runs/day, max pending), ignore bot-origin events, coalescing for latest-state types.
Sample-event check via POST /event-triggers/preview (no work started).

History: work occurrences with event counts and Open/Stop; received events with matched/ignored reason and expandable context; Deliveries log with duplicate counts and Retry recording for recording_failed.
decisions: Separate event-worker service with no Docker socket/model credentials
Delivery identity, logical event identity, match and occurrence are separate durable records
Own-write suppression by correlating successful connector receipts with provider resource versions
Polling for Google/GitHub, Socket Mode for Slack by default
Explicit listening baseline; no historical replay

Event-triggered work via authenticated GitHub and Slack ingestion, general webhooks and Google change detection (subscription or polling), with event deduplication and prevention of self-triggered loops; narrow matching rules preferred over broad listeners.
Events (webhooks, GitHub PRs/issues, Slack messages, workflow failures) start sessions just like prompts or other bots
Room log records turn.started/turn.settled and streams member activity to plugins via on_room_member_activity hook
Separate event-worker collector with only DB/encryption access (no Docker socket, no model credentials).
Use outbound transports (Slack Socket Mode, provider polling with cursors) instead of public webhooks for local operation; signed HTTP supported if ingress exists.

feature:management.title: Recurring management (standing grants on routines/triggers)
feature:management.purpose: A routine or trigger can make its teammate an accountable manager of explicitly selected collaborators under an owner-issued standing grant; scope is frozen per occurrence and intersected with the live grant.
logic: Definition includes optional management {grant_id, targets, operations}; delegate required, manager not a target
validate checks grant kind standing, manager, not revoked/expired, targets/operations subset, collaborators available
At admission bind freezes scope onto work_items.management_scope and inherit sets task grant_id/run ids/management_work_item_id
Occurrence tasks/failure use management_work_item_id so cosmetic reclassification cannot detach work
worker.advance_waiters runs pause_invalid to pause definitions whose grant expired/revoked

Workspace settings > Grants: create standing grant (manager, targets, operations incl. lifecycle ones marked owner-approval, expiry hours, new-bot budget, per-bot memory/CPU caps); list unexpired/standing grants with revoke-and-stop.
Lifecycle proposals arrive as approvals of kind 'lifecycle' showing configuration/before/resources/affected tasks; 'Edit proposal' replaces it via PUT /api/v1/proposals/{id}.
TaskInspector lists teammate proposals and the owner-issued authority (targets/operations/expiry).
Recurring management for routines/triggers uses RecurringManagement to pick or create a delegate standing grant.
decisions: Never auto-select a replacement grant; invalid definitions pause
Static management_work_item_id association

Bot deletion, access-policy changes and credential administration remain owner-only actions; manager-proposed bot creation, configuration and runtime start/stop require owner approval or a matching standing permission, with exact change and resource implications shown before approval and handling for rejection, stale proposals, provisioning failure and partial completion; every management operation is attributed and recorded.

Capability catalog and settings: curated templates, skills, connectors and trusted plugins with prerequisites and permission changes shown before activation; templates are recipes not clones; usage, budgets and export controls.
Roster with avatar, last message, unread, hide, sections and pin; hiding is display-only
Per-session YOLO toggle, context-usage meter, cache hit rate in status bar
Any ordinary bot becomes a manager only via an owner-issued scoped grant (targets, operations, budget, duration); task-bound by default, standing grants for ongoing.
Managers cannot self-escalate, approve on the owner's behalf, read private histories/memory/credentials, gain connector access, or delete bots; stopping a runtime needs separate authority.

Lifecycle proposals show exact config/prior state/resources/affected work; edits create fresh approvals; approved ops go through a durable supervisor outbox; manager resumes after provisioning; retries reuse original identity.
Recurring/event management binds an optional {grant_id, targets, operations} object; server freezes scope at admission; each use intersects with the current grant; no automatic alternate grant.

feature:notifications.title: Web push notifications
feature:notifications.purpose: Bring the owner back when attention items change (questions, reviews, results, problems) via standards Web Push with generic payloads, preferences, quiet hours, batching, and durable fenced delivery; clicks open the current state.
logic: Owner enables push in Notifications: SW registration, PushManager.subscribe, POST subscription (validated, encrypted, device cookie, generation)
Attention projector (notification-worker) materializes new item versions and calls enqueue
enqueue inserts per-subscription deliveries honoring prefs/category/quiet/delay/freshness/overflow
claim rechecks relevance and policy, batches quiet/burst, leases one delivery
deliver sends generic VAPID push through pinned transport, classifies result, retires bad subscriptions
sw.js shows generic notification and routes click to /?attention=<id>
Preference save suppresses pending and re-enqueues under the new revision

Owner menu > Notifications opens settings (10s poll) showing worker health, browser enablement, categories (questions/reviews/results/problems), quiet hours with IANA timezone, and registered browsers.

Enable this browser: checks secure context/Push support/configured keys/permission; requests permission in the click gesture; registers /sw.js; subscribes with the VAPID public key; POSTs the subscription with key_id; turns push_enabled on.
Service worker shows a generic notification and opens /?attention=<id> on click; the app opens the Attention panel at that item.
Disable a device (DELETE subscription) and sign out both clear the local push subscription.
decisions: Generic notification text only; opaque target
Postgres outbox + separate notification-worker; no hosted notification engine
Quiet-hour deferral before transport and generic catch-up summary
pywebpush through PinnedSession

Activity inbox with unread results, questions, approvals and failures; browser push, preferences and quiet hours; duplicate suppression and each notification linked to the correct task; manager summaries link to underlying tasks.
Per-bot notification setting; OS/mobile notifications when a bot finishes or needs input, suppressed while the app is focused; hidden bots never toast but badge a dot
Errors appear above the composer as dismissible notices with request ids; clearing does not undo external actions
Standards Web Push with a small service worker and pywebpush 2.3.0 via Hermbot's constrained pinned-address transport.
Separate notification-worker (control network only, no model/bot credentials) with independent projection and sending pumps.
Push off until explicit opt-in; OS text always generic; details only in authenticated app.

feature:lifecycle.title: Teammate lifecycle and provisioning
feature:lifecycle.purpose: Owner (and, with approval, manager bots) create, edit, clone, archive, restore, start, stop and delete persistent teammates. Every change becomes an immutable bot_operations snapshot that the worker drives through the Docker-owning supervisor, which (re)creates a hardened per-bot container with private network and volumes. UI shows provisioning/error/active status and allows retry.
logic: Owner mutation routes require Idempotency-Key; registry.mutation takes advisory lock on the key and replays/409s via owner_receipts.
validate_config resolves default provider/model, enforces permitted tools, skill names, and 'skills' tool for enabled skills.

register: global advisory lock 887832102, max_bots, id bot-<16hex>, generate bot token + runtime key (Fernet-encrypted, token sha256-hashed), runtime_url http://hermbot-bot-<id>:8642, DM conversation.
reserve_lifecycle fences: human computer control, pending op (incl as clone source), uncertain work; busy work requires interrupt and is cancelled.
owner_operation sets desired_state (stopped for stop/archive/delete), revision+1; delete needs exact name; restore only archived; archived bots can't start/stop.
enqueue snapshots configuration, revision, provider (with secret_encrypted), timezone, desired_state, previous_status, encrypted creds; status -> provisioning|deleting; readiness cleared.
Worker loop: queue_initial bootstraps 'ensure' for active bots with applied_revision<revision; claim leases ops 120 s; drive each.
drive waits while the bot (or clone source) has active/reserved attempts; cancels proposal-backed queued ops whose task/grant ended; marks applying; decrypts and POSTs RuntimeSpec to supervisor.
Supervisor operate: per-bot thread lock, receipt replay by operation_id with request_hash check, execute, fsync receipt + dir, cleanup clone helper.
execute_operation: stop/archive stop the container; delete removes container, helpers, owned volumes and dynamic network; others ensure (clone first when action clone).
ensure: create/verify volumes+network, connect api/worker, fingerprint; recreate container with env/labels/binds/limits/healthcheck; start and wait healthy (75 s).
On success bots.status active/archived/deleted with applied_revision=revision; delete nulls credentials and removes participants; events emitted.
On HTTP failure op failed, bot error with reason; transport errors keep op applying for re-drive.
Owner retry of failed op re-checks revision, busy work, clone source revision and live manager authority without consuming creation budget.
decisions: Only the supervisor holds the Docker socket; API/worker request lifecycle via an authenticated narrow HTTP API with server-owned names/images/mounts.
Durable outbox with immutable payload snapshot and leased workers.
Supervisor receipt files fsynced on a dedicated volume keyed by operation_id with request hash.
Wait for Docker health before reporting success.
Reuse the compose-created volumes/networks for the three core bots under supervisor management.
Recreate the container for each new operation (fingerprint includes operation_id/revision).
One bot owns exactly one container and one persistent Hermes runtime, with separate data volume, workspace, browser profile and resource limits.

Only a container supervisor manages container lifecycle; agent containers never get the Docker socket or another bot's state directory; mounting the same Hermes database into several runtimes is avoided.

Bot lifecycle operations: create, configure, clone, archive, restore, start, stop, delete; cloning copies selected configuration and skills while history, credentials and memory need explicit selection; start with Docker Compose on one host, then dynamic provisioning.
Hermes owns native execution history and agent state; PostgreSQL owns product metadata, task coordination, group transcripts and rebuildable search projections that keep source identifiers.

feature:artifacts.title: Artifacts, file library and attachments
feature:artifacts.purpose: Immutable, checksummed files in MinIO: owner uploads and link imports in a file library with versions and explicit conversation shares; bot-published text/files with task provenance and grants; conversation attachments installed into the recipient's private workspace safely.
logic: Single bucket 'hermbot' created at api startup.
Library save: filename/type/magic validation, preview extraction, version families via advisory locks, object key library/<family>/<id>, insert artifacts.
Bot publish uses uuid5(receipt_id) id; grants publisher task and parent via artifact_access.
publish_file pulls bytes through adapter /workspace/export with integrity checks.
Reads verify size and sha256 (502 on mismatch).
Link import: public IPs only, re-checked per redirect, pinned IP connection, 12 s wall deadline, 10 MB, no compression.
Downloads served with nosniff, no-store and CSP sandbox (PDF frame-ancestors self).
Attachments: uploaded to attachments/<conv>/<id>; installed per attempt through supervisor exec staging and write_attachment.py.
Outputs tab lists conversation artifacts (chat.artifacts) and opens them in the Library at that id.

Library: search by name/text, scope by conversation, 50 per page; upload (<=10MB base64) or import link; detail shows version/size/source/task/SHA-256; preview by content type; Download via /api/v1/artifacts/{id}?download=true.
Versions: 'Add new version' uploads with previous_id; version selector switches selection.
Shares: share selected version with a conversation, revoke share; note that admitted tasks keep their explicit grants.
Use in this conversation: shares then attaches as artifact_ids to the next message (max 10).
Search prior work: GET /api/v1/history/search; result click navigates to the conversation.
decisions: Immutable objects; sharing is explicit per version; revoke blocks new admission only.
Attachments staged via docker exec argv chunks into root-only /run/hermbot-staging.
File bytes for publish_file travel through the adapter, not model arguments.

Artifacts are durable first-class objects in S3-compatible storage with uploads, link ingestion, previews, versions, originating tasks, search, downloads and per-task access grants; bots exchange artifacts by reference without mounting private volumes together; the conversation holds the final result or a link.

Library and structured cards: previews of documents, images, tables and code, editable drafts, and a searchable Library linked to originating conversations; revise existing artifacts rather than creating disconnected copies.
Artifacts are durable outputs bots create or modify (documents, designs, code, data) as a first-class concept alongside bots, chats, prompts and tools
Right-hand preview rail and in-app browser comment/annotate mode with selectors and computed styles for feedback on artifacts
Artifacts are immutable objects in S3-compatible storage (MinIO) with checksums and version families; PostgreSQL holds metadata/grants.
Bots publish existing workspace files through the authenticated runtime adapter (hermbot_publish_file), not through model arguments.
Access by explicit grants: uploads owner-private until shared; shares apply to one version; admitted tasks keep exact version grants after share revocation.

feature:knowledge.title: Native memory and skills
feature:knowledge.purpose: Owner inspects/edits a bot's native Hermes memory and owner-managed hermbot-* skills, enables installed skills, views immutable history, drafts skills from completed work; bots can propose learning that the owner reviews before it is applied.
logic: Adapter reads/writes knowledge files with CAS (sha256 expected hash), flock and atomic replace.
guard requires idle, running, unfenced bot without pending op.
apply validates the full future config before the native write, records knowledge_versions on change, applies config and enqueues 'configure' to refresh Hermes.
Bot hermbot_review(kind skill|memory) freezes payload incl expected hash and revision.
Owner decision: once -> queued; drive_proposals applies under task lock, waits for refresh op completion, then resumes task.
Open from chat header (Memory & skills) or 'Save as skill' on a completed work item (loads /tasks/{id}/skill-draft).
Curated memory: 'User profile' and 'Personal notes' targets; edit with character limit; empty content removes.

Skills: filter, enable/disable (POST .../enabled with expected_revision), open content (bundled read-only), create new from template, import SKILL.md (renamed hermbot-*), save with expected_hash and optional enable.
Saved versions load as drafts; saving creates a new version against the current native hash.
All edits disabled until the runtime is active and running; notice that the runtime refreshes after save.
decisions: Native compare-and-swap plus durable runtime refresh before continuation.
Owner-editable skills limited to hermbot- prefix; bundled skills read-only.

Private bot memory stays private; shared project knowledge is a separate resource bots access deliberately; memory can be inspected, edited, removed and searched; memory is not an authoritative source for changing facts.

Skills: reuse Hermes skills; add create/edit/version/import/enable, save successful workflows as reviewed skills; bots may propose improvements but cannot silently replace approved versions; capability catalog pins executable plugin versions and requires owner authorization.
Bounded curated memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) frozen at session start plus unbounded FTS5 session search and optional external providers
Memory entries scanned for injection/exfiltration patterns and optionally gated by write_approval
Per-bot memory and per-role context, with shared context only via group chats
Do not point two agent processes at the same Hermes home
Memory/skills are native Hermes state edited through Hermbot's private adapter with compare-and-swap, immutable version history and a durable runtime refresh before the next run.
Bot-proposed memory/skill improvements require owner review (editable before approval); Save as skill creates a disabled draft.

feature:tools.title: Capabilities, tool admission and native tool inventory
feature:tools.purpose: Compute and enforce exactly which native and hermbot_* tools a bot may see and execute for its current task; consult enabled skills via hermbot_prepare; expose an owner diagnostic.
logic: Probe records inventory (toolsets, skills with required_tools) into bots.readiness.
manifest derives available/allowed/blocked tools from permissions, inventory version and revision match, intent, grant, human control and connections.
Plugin llm_request filters schemas to allowed_tools; tool_execution middleware re-checks per call through /internal/context.
hermbot_prepare validates requirements and returns raw skill bodies.
Connector ref: handles resolved by tool_references.
Workspace settings 'Permitted tools' (file, terminal, skills, memory, browser, computer_use) bound the per-teammate Tools checkboxes in BotEditor.
Enabled skills are a comma list with datalist of installed skills from GET /bots/{id}/skills (only when runtime running).
CapabilitySummary (Knowledge panel) shows availability per native tool or blocked_tools message, and assigned connections with action counts; notes connections keep native tools available.
decisions: Use existing Hermes llm_request/tool_execution middleware; no upstream patches.
Discovery never grants authority; execution rechecks.
A Hermbot Hermes plugin registers collaboration, orchestration-proposal and artifact tools available in every supported task context (chat, group, routine, connected task).
Per-bot toolsets and MCP enablement are configured through bot settings with the model under advanced settings; model providers are owner-managed with different permitted models per bot.
Tools and skills live at account level while memory and routines belong to the bot
Custom tools should be plugins (tools, hooks, slash commands, capability-gated overrides), not core patches; skills preferred when instructions plus shell suffice
Toolsets as named bundles (core, composite, platform, per-MCP-server) with opt-in workflow-gated toolsets
MCP write-capable tools on untrusted servers require approval consent

Hermes source stays unmodified; integration only via configuration, supported plugin hooks and llm_request/tool_execution middleware plus Hermbot's private runtime adapter; the four earlier source patches were removed.
Connections never disable owner-enabled native tools (terminal/browser/file editing), including for collaborators and revoked connections.

feature:computer.title: Private bot computer, noVNC and takeover
feature:computer.purpose: Each bot has an isolated desktop/browser (TigerVNC, Xfce, Chromium, cua-driver) with persistent browser profile; owner views a thumbnail or live noVNC stream, takes over input exclusively, and hands back explicitly.
logic: Takeover: per-bot advisory lock; require active running bot with no pending op; commit DB fence human first.
Adapter acquires native lease (closes plugin admission), drains admitted tools exclusively, writes ready marker for epoch/viewer.
WS relay api->adapter->RFB unix socket; input filtered until ready; session re-verified every 5 s; disconnect keeps control.
Handback releases native lease; DB fence set agent only when native confirms agent.
Dispatch, context, lifecycle, knowledge and monitor all respect computer_controls.
Open from header Monitor icon or from a secure-input review ('Open computer for secure input').
Polls status (1.5s) and thumbnail (2s); Start computer when stopped.
Expand live view: noVNC RFB to wss/ws same-origin /api/v1/bots/{id}/computer/ws, scaleViewport, view-only unless this session holds input-ready human control; reconnect button after disconnect.
Take over / Reclaim / Confirm control and Hand back (force when another session holds it) via POST computer/control; Stop computer disabled during human control; Open browser only when in control.
Secure input field types characters into the focused remote field via RFB.sendKey and clears immediately; Enter/Tab/Escape helpers.
decisions: Two fences: DB admission fence plus native lease/epoch.
Disconnect never hands back.

Each bot gets its own browser/desktop; the UI exposes three visibility levels (status, pinned preview, full-screen takeover with handback) via an authenticated proxy to Hermes Bot Screen; agent input is suspended during human ownership and ownership persists across disconnect with explicit recovery; browser sessions persist across container recreation.

Browser sessions are bot-specific initially (Hermes Bot Screen default), unlike Grok Bot's shared signed-in browser; sharing logins would need a separate design while connector credentials can be shared via the backend.
Each bot has its own screen with status, preview and takeover levels; human takes control for login/2FA/CAPTCHA/payment then hands back
Screens are work surfaces, not security boundaries; bots share the OS user, files and browser
computer_use approval maps to runtime modes (standard, bounded with reviewed manifest, unrestricted); destructive actions refused when no one can answer and hard-blocked combos exist
Browser work goes through the browser toolset not computer_use; browser sessions persist across handoff
Each bot has its own private desktop/browser environment with a persistent browser-profile volume.
Reuse pinned Hermes Bot Desktop lease/thumbnail/RFB primitives behind an authenticated per-runtime adapter on the private bot network.

feature:auth.title: Owner auth, sessions, service credentials and encryption
feature:auth.purpose: Single-owner authentication by bootstrap token exchanged for opaque revocable cookie sessions; separate credentials for supervisor, each bot and each runtime; persisted credentials encrypted with CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; workspace settings and providers.
logic: verify bearer OWNER_TOKEN or session cookie hash.
login/logout manage owner_sessions and cookies.
Origin check for non-GET and no-store/nosniff headers.
Bot identity by token hash.
Fernet encryption helpers.
Startup refuses short service secrets.
Validation errors never echo inputs.
Login screen asks for the owner token from .env (password field); POST /api/v1/session with Authorization Bearer; the token is discarded from component state.
All requests use same-origin cookies; 401 triggers global reset to login (SSE closed, query cache and idempotency keys cleared).
Sign out: DELETE /api/v1/session, clear browser push, close SSE, clear caches.
Secrets are write-only in UI: provider api_key, OAuth client secret, connection tokens, event source credentials use password inputs with autocomplete off/new-password and are cleared after save.
Workspace settings (timezone, default provider, limits, permitted tools, decision provider, connected app action mode) via GET/PUT /api/v1/settings.
decisions: Opaque server-side sessions over JWT.
Separate Fernet key from service tokens.

Start as a private single-owner app with secure owner login and session management; invited members and owner/admin/member roles come only after the private release; private bots and DMs stay private by default; team bots keep one owning runtime with member-scoped sessions, credentials, workspaces and browser contexts; personal OAuth follows the requesting member.
Private workspace with accounts and invited teammates, no public signup or billing; owner-managed provider credentials
Private bots/DMs first, with explicit sharing of bots and groups later
Team Bot chats stay private per teammate; owner cannot read teammates' chats
Single owner authenticates with OWNER_TOKEN and receives opaque, expiring, revocable HttpOnly/SameSite session cookies.
Provider keys and connector secrets encrypted in PostgreSQL with CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; never returned to the browser.
Owner-managed model providers; bots may use different permitted models; OpenAI-compatible API first, subscriptions later.
.env seeds the initial provider once; owner-edited profiles persist (initial import recorded).

feature:runtime-gate.title: Runtime tool admission gate
feature:runtime-gate.purpose: Make owner computer takeover safe under Hermes's concurrent tool starts: every tool callback holds a shared flock; takeover closes admission via the native lease and drains with an exclusive flock before input is enabled.
logic: admit(): human_holds check, LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB, recheck.
drain(): LOCK_EX polling with ownership checks and 70 s timeout.
Plugin wraps every tool in admit; reports pause.
Adapter control uses drain then ready marker.
Computer panel shows lease holder and 'Waiting for in-flight work to settle' until input_ready; 'Bot tools and new dispatch remain paused until handback' when admission_paused.
Status label waiting_computer = 'Waiting for computer handback'; CapabilitySummary asks to hand back the computer; TaskActivity shows tool.admitted 'admitted; waiting to start'.
phase3_inflight.py proves takeover waits for a running foreground tool (>4s) and the effect runs once after handback; phase3_recovery_driver injects worker pause/restart and runtime recreation.
decisions: Shared per-callback admission instead of exclusive mutex.

Approvals come from real runtime requests, shown as structured action cards with approve/deny/expiry/cancel; external writes require approval unless covered by an explicit standing permission; secure input stays outside transcripts; unknown action scopes pause for review; managers collect required reviews but cannot approve on the user's behalf.
Wrap the Hermes runtime through its API server (runs, sessions, jobs, skills/toolsets discovery) bearer-gated by API_SERVER_KEY with per-profile scoping
Profiles are not a sandbox; real isolation requires container/terminal backends
Bot Mode protocol injection requires exact title 'Bot Chat' plus a ui_meta hermes-bots marker, so headless installs must write both

Per-bot runtime gate with shared nonblocking admission for concurrent tool callbacks; exclusive drain only when takeover closes admission; exact viewer/epoch gates readiness; timeouts keep input disabled.
Worker/API restarts reconnect existing run identities without replaying uncertain actions.
Hermes source unmodified; four patches replaced by supported middleware and private adapter

feature:testing.title: Test architecture, protocol fixture and acceptance evidence
feature:testing.purpose: Verify Hermbot at four boundaries: (1) a pytest regression suite against an isolated PostgreSQL database hermbot_test (plus MinIO) with fakes for Docker, Hermes runtime RPC and providers; (2) a deterministic OpenAI-compatible protocol fixture model that drives real pinned Hermes runtimes via compose.protocol.yaml; (3) owner-authorized live acceptance drivers that use the paid configured model and sometimes real connected accounts, writing manifest/evidence JSON into test-results/; (4) Playwright browser scripts (real or mocked API) that write screenshots and JSON. Read-only audits (scripts/*_audit.py) re-verify saved evidence against current state.
logic: scripts/check.py starts postgres+storage, creates hermbot_test if missing, builds hermbot-tools:phase1 from backend/Tools.Dockerfile, runs ruff over backend/plugins/docker/tests/scripts, then pytest -q --junitxml=/app/test-results/backend.xml inside the tools container on hermbot_control with DATABASE_URL rewritten to hermbot_test.
pytest config: testpaths=tests; markers integration/hermes/live declared.

tests/conftest.py session fixture exits unless DATABASE_URL ends with /hermbot_test, runs db.initialize(); per-test autouse fixture truncates tables, reseeds preferences, resets the 3 seed bots/workspace settings and patches worker.settings; make_task factory creates tasks via service.create_task.

Fakes: native.request (runtime adapter RPC), connector_providers.execute, provisioning.supervisor, containers.docker_request/runtime_command, notifications.send/PinnedSession.post, socket/HTTP servers on loopback; real plugin and docker/*.py modules loaded from /app via importlib.

Protocol stack: compose.protocol.yaml adds service model-fixture (uvicorn tests.model_fixture:app :8010 on the three bot networks) and points MODEL_BASE_URL/MODEL_NAME of api, worker and the hermes-* services to it; prompt markers [POC:*] script tool calls.

Acceptance drivers (python -m tests.<driver>) call http://api:8000 with OWNER_TOKEN, submit each request with an Idempotency-Key (often twice to prove dedupe), persist a manifest before mutations, support resumable modes (start/status/continue/verify/cleanup), and verify via API plus direct DB reads (tool_receipts, events, result_acceptances).

Operator-in-the-loop: recovery drivers write test-results/recovery-signal.json and poll for recovery-<name>-done markers created after the operator performs the Docker action; browser phase2-work/phase3-ui-fixes use the same pattern served by scripts/phase3_recovery_driver.py.

Browser checks: Node ESM scripts with playwright 1.56.1, log in via the Owner token form, either drive real flows or intercept /api/v1/* with page.route to inject fixtures, assert no page errors and no horizontal overflow across viewports, write PNG/JSON to /output.

Evidence export/audit: tests/export_evidence.py aggregates durable receipts into execution-evidence.json; scripts/*_audit.py (phase2/3/4, skills_tools, native_tools, work_outcomes, routines_final/integrity) perform read-only re-verification and upstream-source comparisons.
Verifier self-tests: tests/test_phase4_acceptance_evidence.py and tests/test_event_provider_acceptance.py unit-test the acceptance verification helpers so the harness cannot produce false positives.
scripts/check.py runs ruff + pytest in hermbot-tools against hermbot_test and writes test-results/backend.xml, which every audit reads for test counts/failures.
Audit scripts cross-check saved test-results evidence JSON against live API state and Docker inspection; acceptance drivers create fixtures through the owner API and write proof manifests.
UI is exercised by Playwright scripts in tests/browser (e.g. ui-regressions, work-items, routines, event-triggers, phase3-computer), referenced by audits via test-results JSON.
decisions: Separate deterministic protocol acceptance from live-model acceptance
Every pytest test runs against real PostgreSQL (autouse fixture) rather than SQLite/mocks
Acceptance drivers are resumable, manifest-first and never resubmit lost work
Owner/human performs irreversible or privileged actions (approvals of real writes, Docker restarts, OS push permission, secure input)
Use container paths (/app, /opt/hermes, /output) in tests and drivers

Phases deliver usable capability, preserve earlier acceptance tests and close only on exit gates; POC is the first working increment of the final architecture with real containers, not a mock; cumulative matrix covers collaboration, orchestration, management, authority, execution, recovery, external actions, artifacts, routines, computer, UI and team access; use deterministic fake providers/connectors for failure paths plus real Hermes/model runs for acceptance; test real connectors with read-only and approved writes.

Phase 1 POC proves manual and autonomous collaboration across research/writing, data processing and code/review, from chats, groups and one-shot scheduled tasks, plus manager orchestration with injected recoverable failure, redirect and cancellation, and failure handling (browser disconnect, container restart, duplicate delivery, pending approval).
Verification at every milestone with lint, typecheck, tests and build; plan file as source of truth plus status/decisions doc
Doctor-style triage command for environment checks (computer-use doctor with exit codes)
Deterministic fakes exercise failure paths; acceptance requires real Hermes/model runs; synthetic responses never count as live acceptance.

feature:ops.title: Operational tooling (configure, upgrade, check, stop, notification keys, audits, acceptance drivers)
feature:ops.purpose: Host-side Python scripts that create and upgrade the private .env without printing secrets, run the isolated test suite in containers, stop the stack safely, generate VAPID keys, and produce/verify acceptance evidence (test-results/*.json) against the live local workspace and Docker state.
logic: Bootstrap: configure.py creates .env exclusively (0600) with random tokens/passwords and CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY; compose refuses to start until those exist.
Upgrade: upgrade_config.py appends CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY and PUBLIC_URL only if missing and re-chmods 0600.
Push keys: notification_setup.py --contact mailto:... generates a P-256 VAPID pair once (preserves an existing private key), then api and notification-worker must be recreated.
Checks: check.py starts postgres/storage, ensures hermbot_test, builds hermbot-tools, runs ruff and pytest (junit to test-results/backend.xml) on hermbot_control.
Stop: stop.py stops the worker first (prevents desired-state reconciliation restarting bots), then labelled managed runtimes, then all compose services; volumes preserved.

Audits (read-only): phase2/phase3/phase4, native_tools, skills_tools, work_outcomes, routines_final, routines_integrity verify saved evidence vs live API (owner Bearer token read from .env), artifact sha256, container image/volume/hardening, upstream Hermes source unchanged, and write *-audit.json proofs.

Acceptance drivers (mutating, staged): phase3_inflight, phase3_browser_persistence, phase3_recovery_driver (signal files), group_work_history (--apply), event_trigger_acceptance and event_provider_acceptance (stage argv; proof manifest guards against duplicate fixtures).
decisions: Scripts never print credential values; audits project Docker inspect output without container environments.
Stop the worker before the runtimes in stop.py.
Acceptance drivers persist a proof manifest before mutation and refuse to re-run setup when it exists.
Tests run in a separate hermbot_test database inside a pinned tools container.
Failure injection in phase3_recovery_driver validates container labels and limits targets to researcher/writer.

Deployment on Docker Compose (dev and initial single server), PostgreSQL-backed work queues instead of a separate message broker, SSE for durable events with cursor reconnect plus WebSockets for computer and voice transport, pinned images, containerized dev tooling because Node is not installed locally.

Release hardening phase: consistent backups of Postgres, object storage and each bot's runtime state with restore on a clean host, graceful drain and upgrades, correlated logs with support identifiers, monitoring of queue age/stuck approvals/container health, resource and spending limits, extended unattended run and provider-outage tests, runbooks.

Defaults and boundaries: start with three bots, validate release with ten registered bots and three active tasks, groups up to six, English UI with localization-ready resources; no public signup, billing, native mobile or desktop packaging; model quality evaluated separately from UI/workflow parity.
Run Hermes in Docker (nousresearch/hermes-agent) with data volume, s6 supervision per profile and moderate resource limits (1-4GB, 1-2 CPU); Chromium is the heaviest
Local POC first then always-on Linux server; Docker locally

feature:intake.title: Message intake, work items and revisions
feature:intake.purpose: The owner just sends chat messages. Hermbot decides, before any bot executes, whether a message is discussion, a status question, a new assignment, an update to existing work, an answer to a pending question, a cancellation or a routine draft. It records concrete required results and owner-quoted authorizations, keeps one work card per requested outcome across many messages and bots, and delivers revisions to running or waiting executions. Cards can be hidden/restored without touching execution.
logic: POST /api/v1/messages (intent auto by default) creates the carrier task (status queued, orchestration_version=2, coordination_version=1, intake_status pending) and the owner message in one transaction, idempotent on Idempotency-Key.
claim_new never dispatches a v2 task while message_intent is still 'auto', so nothing executes before interpretation.

work_intake.advance_one (worker background loop) claims the oldest pending auto task per conversation (FIFO: no earlier pending task in the same conversation) with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a 60s lease.

Evidence is assembled: latest owner message, 60 recent messages, pending questions, up to 30 candidate work items with outcomes, saved routines, standing grants, supported connector actions, current time, JSON schema.

The receiving bot's provider/model is called at {base_url}/chat/completions with json_object response, optional read_context tool (<=3 calls per round), up to 4 rounds within 45s; schema/alignment validation errors are fed back as system messages.
apply() re-locks the task, refuses if the owner edited the message (hash) or any observed work revision changed, then forces owner_work_target when the message came from Redirect/edit/answer.
Each operation beyond the first gets a derived task (request_key intake:{task}:{index}) inheriting grant, files and thread, so one message can both answer and revise work.
Routine intent saves an inactive draft after quote/conversation/bot checks; the carrier becomes discussion with a continuation telling the bot to point at the draft.
Cancel intent cancels non-terminal roots of the work item and supersedes all its requirements.

Other intents go through work_items.route(intake=True): assignment -> new_item; update -> fences (unless intake), reuse responsible participant when previous root settled, or mark 'steered' when an active root exists; status/discussion just tag the message.
Assignment/update then call work_controller.apply with requirements (nulls preserve existing target/dependencies/required), supersede_keys and requested_effects.

work_controller.apply is idempotent per (work item, source owner message, kind), supersedes requirements (invalidating undispatched drafts and authorizations), registers requirements with owner_revision=True, bumps work revision, records authorizations whose quote is a substring of the owner message, writes work_changes, and emits 'revise' commands for every other non-terminal task of the work item.

Commands are written to work_commands and to controls (same id) in the same transaction; work_controller.advance/reconcile later refreshes bindings, admits matching connector drafts and wakes waiting tasks that have pending owner directions.
Intake marks every carrier intake_status applied with intake_result and emits message.interpreted; clarification becomes a continuation instructing the bot to ask.
decisions: Interpret owner messages in the backend with a structured model call before execution, instead of letting the receiving bot route via hermbot_route_message.
Only the latest authenticated owner message is a source of authority; requested_effects and routine proposals must quote it verbatim.
Optimistic concurrency: apply only if message hash and observed work revisions are unchanged since evidence was gathered; no DB transaction held across the model call.
Per-conversation FIFO intake.
Revisions are delivered as durable commands + controls written in the same transaction as the revision.
Work items are independent of execution trees; message association changes never stop/replay execution.
Bot creation is by describing a role (name, role, avatar, model, capability config), with focused single-job bots recommended; first-run flow covers create bot, connect app, give first task.
Direct user messages take priority over background work and can redirect the current turn; queue vs steer is a deliberate choice
Idempotency-keyed run creation for retry-safe intake over the runtime API
Ordinary messages are interpreted automatically; no message-intent dropdown, work selector or skill picker in the composer.

feature:outcomes.title: Required results, evidence and result acceptance
feature:outcomes.purpose: Execution completion is not work completion. Each work item records versioned required results (report, artifact, connector_effect, execution_check, native_effect). Bots submit claims with hermbot_finish; the backend applies them only after the run settles and only with suitable evidence (provider receipts, accessible artifacts, reviewed contributions, tool execution evidence). The card shows partial progress, needs-answer/needs-approval/uncertain states, and the owner can drop requirements or reconcile uncertain native effects.
logic: Requirements are registered by intake (owner_revision) or, for legacy v0/v1 work, by the root task's hermbot_prepare.outcomes; keys unique, dependency graph acyclic, provenance = owner message.

Changing a requirement bumps its revision and resets it to pending; needs expected_revision; non-owner changes need a new owner update; fulfilled external effects immutable; owner revisions invalidate undispatched drafts and authorizations (retaining them if destination unchanged).
Root tasks are bound to all outcomes (task_outcomes with revision); children get only outcomes shared at delegation.
Coordination v1: each outcome gets an accountable owner_task_id (first live root assignment) and delegations create contributions or transfer the deliverable.
hermbot_publish/publish_file stores an artifact; if bound to an artifact/report outcome with ready dependencies it records evidence (or acceptance); otherwise supporting evidence only.

Connector actions bind to an unfinished connector_effect outcome and its revision; settlement of the operation calls effect_settled (succeeded -> record; denied/failed -> blocked; uncertain/unresolved -> uncertain).
hermbot_finish converts results-by-key into claims, validates them provisionally, and stores pending_result/pending_outcomes; nothing is fulfilled yet.

When the runtime settles, worker.settle calls outcomes.settle: non-completed runs fail unfinished assigned outcomes (except v2 helpers); completed runs re-validate claims in a savepoint and record each; any validation error rejects the whole batch (work.evidence_rejected).

record(): with an accountable owner it goes through result_acceptance.record: contributors' fulfilments become 'submitted' contributions; the owner's fulfilment validates contributions/reviews/read_artifact receipts and inserts a result_acceptances row (UNIQUE per outcome revision) then marks the outcome fulfilled.

Work status projection: uncertain > budget pause > (legacy fallback) > needs_answer > uncertain ops > needs_approval > working > completed (all required fulfilled) > cancelled > task stop states > needs_attention > working/planning.

Owner drop: versioned cancel of an unfulfilled requirement (v2 also invalidates drafts, revokes auth, cancels questions, records owner action); owner reconcile: uncertain native_effect -> fulfilled/failed/uncertain with owner evidence.
Budget interruption after a native tool started marks unconfirmed native_effect outcomes uncertain.

Work card summary 'X of Y required results ready' from item.progress; each outcome shows status, optional flag, reason, evidence strength label (reviewed artifact / provider receipt / artifact exists / model reported / owner attested), contributions and acceptance review.
Remove this requirement: mutate POST /api/v1/outcomes/{id}/drop {expected_revision}.
decisions: Separate work item, requirement, task/attempt, connector operation, question and approval records.
Apply claims only after the run settles, in a savepoint, validating the whole batch.
Evidence strength is explicit (provider_receipt, artifact_exists, reviewed_artifact, model_reported, owner_attested).
Accountable owner accepts shared deliverables; contributions cannot fulfil them; accepted file contributions require a read_artifact receipt.
Native external effects (browser/terminal) cannot be accepted by model claim; they need owner reconciliation.
Distinguish a logical task from an execution run: a run may finish while its task awaits a teammate or human decision; task status, delegation tree and results are first-class API objects.

Do not claim universal exactly-once external execution; use durable identities and provider idempotency where available, surface uncertain outcomes, and reconcile existing receipts/provider state before any retry.
Treat the form of an answer as part of the answer: inline cards for drafts, routines created, settings changed, bot-to-bot messages
Plan then goal: plans answer how, goals answer what must be true before done; durable goals persist across turns
Separate record types: work item, required outcome, task/attempt, connector operation, human question, approval; extend the existing work item instead of a new workflow system.

feature:coordination.title: Teammate coordination: messages, delegation, waits, replacement
feature:coordination.purpose: Teammates collaborate through backend-mediated tools. hermbot_message queues a scoped, non-blocking inbox message; hermbot_delegate creates an asynchronous child assignment (contribution or deliverable transfer); hermbot_wait names results actually required and releases execution capacity; failures wake the responsible teammate; settled unsuccessful contributions can be replaced. Legacy (coordination v0) delegation blocks the parent in waiting_children and resumes it with child results.
logic: hermbot_delegate -> tool_action -> service.delegate: bot running, no self-delegation, grant allows delegate, depth < MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH, no ancestor cycle, root handoffs < min(MAX_HANDOFFS, grant), outcome ids required (v2 defaults to all unfinished assigned), sibling dependencies, granted artifacts/attachments, skill capability check.

Child task inserted queued (or blocked with dependencies) with handoff brief, same work item/intent/versions, grant inherited; task_outcomes shared; coordination v1 -> result_acceptance.assign creates contribution or transfers deliverable; dependencies rows; artifact_access; root handoffs+1.
Legacy: parent set waiting_children; v1: parent continues running.
hermbot_message (v1) -> coordination.send: recipient running, conversation participant or work collaborator or grant target; reply_to must address this bot; teammate_messages pending.
Busy recipient: /internal/context returns teammate_inbox; plugin llm_request injects it and calls /internal/inbox-delivered to mark delivered to the current attempt.

Idle recipient: claim_new first runs schedule_inboxes, which creates one internal peer_message discussion task per recipient/conversation/work for unanswered messages (or delivered ones whose attempt settled) and links response_task_id.
hermbot_wait -> coordination.wait: only directly owned child tasks (no same-bot, no wait cycle) or messages sent by this task; coordination_waits rows; task -> waiting_results.
At settlement a v1 task with unaccepted required contributions or an explicit wait stays waiting_results (capacity released).

advance_waiters -> coordination.advance: for each waiting_results task without active attempt, evaluate waits (child status/dependency_ready, replies, failed responses) and required contributions; requeue with a data-only continuation when nothing pending or something failed and the signature changed; clear waits when not pending.
Contributor finish submits contribution (result_acceptance.record), accountable owner then accepts with reviewed_task_ids and read_artifact receipts.

Replacement: delegate with replaces_task_id supersedes a settled failed/interrupted/cancelled contribution preserving required flag; manager reassign (grant op) replaces a failed child, rewires waits/dependencies/contributions.

Legacy dependencies: blocked children released in advance_waiters when all parents dependency_ready, with dependency outputs and artifact grants in continuation; waiting_children parents resume when children terminal (or actionable failure) and signature differs from observed_terminal_children.
Read access: hermbot_read_artifact only for artifacts produced by or granted to the task; status/work_status expose public assignment state.
'Coordinate team' switch sends managed_bot_ids (<=9 selected peers) and, with 'Allow lifecycle proposals for owner review', management_operations incl. create/configure/start/stop.
decisions: Informational messages are non-blocking inbox entries separate from assignments.
Explicit waits release execution capacity.
Peer replies to idle recipients run as internal discussion executions that cannot spawn reply loops.
Manager authority is a grant scoped to targets/operations; delegation never transfers credentials or private state.
All application-managed bot-to-bot communication goes through a Hermbot Hermes plugin plus a backend coordination service rather than relying on Hermes native message_agent/hermes peer alone.

Delegation is asynchronous: a waiting parent releases its execution slot and the worker delivers child results and resumes the parent continuation; bounded depth (3), at most 10 automatic handoffs per chain, budgets and cancellation propagation.

Communication contract distinguishes message, task request and task result with stable IDs, sender, recipient, originating conversation, deadline and status; delivery acknowledgement means accepted, not finished; reconcile an existing request before resubmitting.

Manager orchestration: a manager is an ordinary bot with a scoped management grant (targets, operations, budget, duration); managers plan, assign, monitor, redirect, recover and finish work; cannot self-escalate; relationship does not reveal private conversations, credentials or memory; stopping a whole runtime needs separate authority; configuration changes apply between runs; reassignment reconciles the old attempt first.
Group rooms of 2 to 6 bots with bounded serial rounds (3) and message caps (10), @mention scoping, bots may pass, @user escalation raising needs-you
Bot-to-bot handoff via asynchronous message_agent with attribution, delivery ids, typed failure reasons and at-most-one retry for transient errors

feature:execution.title: Execution dispatch, policy, budgets, monitoring, stop/redirect/retry and recovery
feature:execution.purpose: Runs teammate work on per-bot Hermes runtimes continuously until completion, a real wait, Stop, an owner deadline or the shared active budget. The worker admits queued tasks one per bot under global capacity, dispatches native runs with stable idempotency keys, streams events, accounts active time, delivers decisions and directions, settles results, recovers safely after restarts, and refuses to replay anything whose effect may have happened (uncertain).
logic: claim_new: global advisory lock; capacity max_active - active/reserved attempts; per bot: active+running+provider+applied revision, no human computer control, readiness compatible, no pending lifecycle op, no active attempt; oldest queued eligible task.
Lock order with SKIP LOCKED: trigger locks, routine definition, work item, root task, bot row; then locked_task and recheck queued.
Preflight: routine/trigger start_allowed, pending connector ops -> waiting_approval, grant valid (else cancel), deadline (cancel kind deadline), budget (pause).

Native session per conversation/bot or per thread; prompt = continuation or input + thread context + skills + handoff brief + occurrence scope + attachments + granted files + pending owner/manager controls; instructions MANAGED_POLICY(v2)/POLICY + COORDINATION_POLICY.
Insert attempt 'dispatching' with Idempotency-Key hermbot:{attempt_id}, 12s lease; controls/work_commands included; task running, attempts+1, continuation/pending cleared; event task.started.

drive: copy attachments, ensure native session, POST /v1/runs (Idempotency-Key), store runtime_run_id; account time; pause if budget exhausted; stop if stopping; start event stream; GET /v1/runs/{id} status.
Terminal status -> settle; budget exhausted -> pause; else deliver decided runtime approvals (POST /approval) and one pending control (POST /steer), then queue a monitor assessment.
settle maps runtime terminal to task state (see sm:task), with bounded automatic recovery for retryable failures before any tool ran and complete event coverage (MAX_RECOVERIES).

Budgets: shared per work item (assignment/update) or per root; account() charges only while observed running; pause() moves tree to pausing_budget/paused_budget; Continue adds the workspace allowance after fences.

Monitor: when decision_mode enabled and a run is silent 180s or repeats tool failures, queue an assessment; separate loop claims it, re-validates currency, calls decisions.assess; with decision_actions and confidence>=0.85 inserts a monitor control (never stops/approves).

Stop: service.cancel stops descendants (attempts -> stopping; tasks cancelling or cancelled, uncertain kept), cancels pending reviews/questions/proposals/ops; drive sends POST /v1/runs/{id}/stop; settle preserves the owner's stop reason.
Redirect: service.steer; v2 creates an auto-intake message targeted at the work (revision path), legacy inserts a control delivered via native steer or next continuation.
Retry (owner): only settled failed/interrupted/cancelled, not all required fulfilled, no unknown connector outcome, whole tree settled; creates a new task (v2 via intake with owner_work_target).

Restart recovery: claim_existing re-leases attempts with expired lease; drive reuses runtime_run_id (poll) or re-POSTs with same idempotency key (<23h); 404 for accepted run -> uncertain; streams resume with gap flag.
decisions: PostgreSQL is the queue (advisory lock + SKIP LOCKED + leases), not a broker.
One active/uncertain attempt per bot enforced by a partial unique index.
Never automatically replay an effect that may have happened; mark uncertain.
Budgets measure active execution time shared across teammates and revisions of a work item, not wall-clock.
Execution monitoring is advisory and opt-in.

Use Hermes authenticated Runs/HTTP-SSE API (or JSON-RPC gateway) for execution, streaming events, steering, stop and approvals via an adapter; probe the installed version and choose transport per workflow.

Default one active execution per bot; queued human instructions are preserved, never silently dropped; direct human messages take priority and can redirect the current turn; stop semantics cascade to children.
Background execution requires an always-on Linux host: develop locally in Docker then move the same architecture to a persistent server; the browser closing must not stop execution.
Background run model: runs with SSE events, stop, steer, approval endpoints; detached completions never start unsolicited model turns
Cron-style execution is not an exactly-once side-effect guarantee

feature:attention.title: Owner questions, approvals/reviews, decisions and attention inbox
feature:attention.purpose: Separates information requests (typed questions with answers) from permission for exact actions (approvals), resolves them through authenticated owner endpoints or ordinary chat, closes stale prompts without inventing decisions, and projects everything needing the owner (questions, reviews, results, problems, setup) into a durable versioned attention inbox that drives badges and optional push.
logic: hermbot_ask (or legacy review kind=input) -> inputs.ask: validate choices, dedupe by question hash, fence other reviews/ops, insert input_request (expiry min(24h, deadline)), task waiting_input.
Owner answers via card (POST /api/v1/input-requests/{id}/answer) or chat (intake answer_question -> work_items.route answer uses the actual owner text for text questions).

inputs.answer locks task+question, checks hash/type/expiry/stop/conversation/grant/outcome revision, records answer idempotently, appends continuation, requeues unless an attempt is still active; for v2 owner answers creates an auto-intake task and sets resume_after_intake so the original waits for interpretation.

hermbot_review -> request_review: rejects connector-shaped generic reviews, fences pending question/op/review, prepares knowledge/connector payloads, validates secure input, inserts approval with payload hash and expiry, task waiting_approval.
Runtime command approvals come from the Hermes event stream (approval.request) and are inserted idempotently by source_id.

Owner decides (POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}) with payload hash; repeat of same decision idempotent; secure input requires computer handed back; kind dispatch to knowledge/connections/lifecycle; generic kinds write guidance continuation and requeue; runtime decisions delivered by deliver_decisions to /v1/runs/{id}/approval.
Owner edits a review (PUT): old approval and its pending drafts superseded, new review created and linked.

reconcile_requests (on settle and every loop) closes pending approvals/questions when the task closed, expired or a runtime approval's attempt ended; an expiry stops waiting work (kind review_expired).
owner_requests.valid is the shared actionability predicate for /state, inputs.pending and attention.

Attention: DB triggers mark subjects dirty in attention_pending inside source transactions; notification worker drains (try-lock), projects task (questions/reviews/legacy result/problem), work (result only when completed and fully settled; problem states) and source setup items; materialize bumps version on fingerprint change and enqueues push; close_missing deactivates stale items.
Inbox API pages needs/updates/history with counts in one statement; read/dismiss/unread only the observed versions; dismiss cannot clear live owner decisions.
Sidebar 'Attention' row shows unread and needs-you counts from GET /api/v1/attention?limit=1 (5s).
Attention panel tabs Needs you / Updates / History with cursor paging; Mark read/unread/Dismiss (dismiss hidden for active owner-needed items); Mark visible read.

Detail resolves the live source; if still active it embeds the InputCard or the same ApprovalCard used in chat; Open work navigates to the conversation/thread and opens TaskInspector; settings-type items open Connections or Routines/Event triggers.
decisions: Typed questions are separate from approvals.
Closing a prompt never records an owner decision; expiry stops waiting work rather than resuming as if answered.
Attention invalidation via DB triggers in the same transaction (transactional outbox) with generation counters, level-based reconciliation, no max(event id) watermark.
Reading never authorizes; read_version only advances to the version presented.

Present each bot with presence/state from the avatar (idle, thinking, working, waiting, blocked, done) with hover detail, and distinguish working, unread results, questions, approvals and failures; status wording must differentiate working, waiting-for-me and failed.
Avatar carries lifecycle state (idle/thinking/working/waiting/blocked/done) with hover for current action instead of step logs
Sidebar distinguishes needs-attention (question/approval/handoff) from unread activity from working
Ordinary questions are persistent typed input requests separate from approvals; an answer never grants permission and an approval supplies no answer text.
Reviews bind an exact payload/hash; editing creates a new approval and supersedes the old (HTTP 409 on stale); managers request but cannot approve.
Attention is a durable current-state view separating source state, owner read state and transport state; reading/dismissing never answers or approves.

feature:conversations.title: Conversations: DMs, groups, threads, transcripts, live updates
feature:conversations.purpose: Owner chats with teammates in one DM per bot or in groups of 2-6 bots. Messages can be threaded (separate native sessions), carry attachments, mentions, skill refs and library files. The UI loads paginated transcripts with reactions, receives live updates through SSE, and can read the authoritative native Hermes history.
logic: DM per bot is bootstrapped (unique index one_dm_per_bot); groups created with >=2 distinct registered bots.
Every owner submission inserts a user message with source_id request:{task_id}; bot results insert assistant messages runtime-result:{attempt_id}; both idempotent via ON CONFLICT(source_id).
Threads: reply_to_message_id normalized to the thread root; worker maps thread root+bot to its own native session (thread_sessions) and prefixes the parent message as quoted context.
Mentions must be participants; stored on the owner message.
Attachments must belong to the conversation; worker lists them in the prompt and provisioning copies them into the bot workspace before the run.
Transcript API returns 100 messages per page (before cursor, thread filter) with work association, reply counts, reactions, artifacts, attachments.
Live updates: SSE /api/v1/events polls events every 0.5s; UI EventSource appends message.delta text to partial bubbles and debounces invalidation of state/chat/attention queries.
Archived conversations disappear from /state and block new work, peer messages and attention.
Native history proxied from Hermes /api/sessions/{id}/messages (authoritative incl. compacted).
Reactions toggle, group edit/removal, conversation archive/restore and attachment upload are in product.py.
Sidebar: teammates (DMs), past teammates, groups; sections collapsible and persisted in localStorage 'hermbot-sidebar-sections'; search expands all sections.
Groups: create/edit (2-6 members, title <=120) via POST /api/v1/groups or PUT /api/v1/groups/{id}; remove via DELETE (saved work remains).
Transcript: markdown messages with byline, edited marker, 'saved routine instructions' label for routine-revision sources, mentions, attachment download links, Reply (thread) and 👍 reactions.
Threads: opening a message sets ?thread=<id> on the conversation query and replies send reply_to_message_id.
decisions: Hermes owns native session history; Hermbot stores its own transcript of owner messages and final results.
Reply threads use separate native sessions.
SSE is a DB-poll invalidation channel; UI re-fetches state.

Bots, not chats, are the primary navigation objects: a roster of persistent teammates, each with a permanent conversation; threads, reactions, mentions, skill references, attachments, queued messages, steer/stop and visible retry.

Group chats of up to six bots with attributed messages, @mention routing, membership editing and human escalation; a single authoritative room history and exactly one active server-side driver per room that decides whose turn runs; limits on rounds, time and spending; the browser never owns group execution.

Message UX: structured progress is derived from real runtime events, never invented text; duplicate clicks and reconnects must not resubmit; reopening restores active run, partial output and pending approvals.
One permanent canonical Bot Chat per bot; /new compacts rather than forks; archiving retires and starts a fresh canonical chat
Composer features borrowed from Grok Bot: / for saved skills, @ for bots/groups/routines/connectors, reply/thread/react, steering while work runs, editable drafts before send, Stop now
Heterogeneous transcript where conversation, system events, interactive cards and visualizations share one timeline
The browser never drives execution; one authoritative server-side transcript/driver per room; closing the client doesn't stop work.

flow:c.title: Connector action > review/approval > provider call > receipt/reconciliation
flow:c.summary: A bot calls hermbot_connector; reads run inline; mutations are frozen into a review (or matched to an owner request/standing permission), queued after Allow once, dispatched by the task worker with a committed dispatching marker, and settled with a definitive receipt or left uncertain for owner reconciliation.
steps: Bot tool hermbot_connector posts to /internal/tools; app.tools validates arguments and calls service.tool_action
tool_action resolves the connection and, for mutations, requires a work item; then calls connections.invoke
invoke authorizes bot/action, resolves remembered references, validates arguments against the fixed catalog and resource allow-list

Read: get credential (refresh if near expiry), call fixed provider endpoint via pinned transport, redact, remember references (or import Drive file to library); auth failure marks needs_reconnect and pauses event sources
Mutation: reject if task already has an unfinished op; resolve outcome; prepare_review freezes payload with connection revision and outcome revision
If an owner-requested authorization or a standing permission matches, insert a queued operation directly and set task waiting_approval
Otherwise service.request_review creates an approval (payload hash) and record_review inserts a pending connector_operations row
Attention trigger marks the task dirty; owner sees the review (flow:g)
Owner decides POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}: once -> op queued after connection revision recheck; deny/cancel -> denied, outcome settled, bot resumed. Edit (PUT) supersedes op and creates a new review
Task worker loop calls drive_one each iteration; under global advisory lock it marks stale dispatching ops uncertain and selects one queued op whose task has no active attempt

Under per-connection advisory lock, task lock and connection row lock, recheck grant, bot/action, task state/expiry, revision, resource, outcome state/dependencies, payload hash and approval/authorization/standing budget; failures finish as failed
Commit status dispatching with 120s lease in a separate transaction before the provider sees the request; increment standing permission use
Call MCP tools/call or the fixed provider adapter with operation-derived identifiers
finish_operation records succeeded/failed/uncertain, settles the outcome effect, emits connector.<status> and resumes the bot with a definitive receipt (uncertain does not resume)
Worker claim gate keeps a task with unfinished connector ops in waiting_approval
Owner reconciles uncertain ops in Connections > Activity (succeeded/failed with evidence, or unresolved after stopping) without replay
Successful receipts later feed own-write suppression for event triggers

flow:d.title: Routine tick > admission > run > history
flow:d.summary: Saved routine revisions bind a per-bot wake token; the task worker installs a Hermes no-agent 1-minute cron job in the bot runtime that posts a scoped wake; the API ticks due routines, admits idempotent occurrences into ordinary tasks; the worker first-claim gate rechecks; history derives status from work items.
steps: Owner saves routine via POST /api/v1/routines (app.py) or PUT /api/v1/routines/{id}; idempotent owner mutation; chat intake may save an inactive draft
save validates access (incl. management grant), inserts owner source message and immutable revision, sets state/next_run_at, cancels unstarted runs on revision change, ensures scheduler binding
Task worker runs routines.run; every 10s reconcile_schedulers computes wanted (any active routine) and PUTs generation/token/enabled to the bot runtime
runtime_api writes hermbot_routine_wakeup.py and hermbot-routine-wakeup.json {url, token}, creates/pauses/resumes the Hermes cron job "Hermbot wake <generation>" (every 1m, --no-agent)
Each minute Hermes runs the script, which POSTs {} with the bearer token to /internal/routine-wake/{bot}/{generation}
wake verifies generation and token hash, records last_tick_at and ticks if enabled
tick locks up to 50 due active routines for the bot (SKIP LOCKED); pauses after 3 definite failures or archived destination; records a gap row and applies catch-up latest after downtime

admit dedupes occurrence (and same scheduled_at across revisions), checks overlap, start window, daily cap and access; inserts admitted/skipped run with reason and frozen context (+since_success window)

admit creates a system thread message and, in a savepoint, create_saved_task: service.create_task (orchestration v2), budget, management bind, work_controller.apply requirements/effects; failure -> skipped
tick advances next_run_at (or state finished when none)
Worker claim_new locks the routine definition (SKIP LOCKED) and calls start_allowed which cancels if paused/archived/revised/destination archived/start window missed/access invalid
Execution proceeds as ordinary work (flow:a); pause_invalid in advance_waiters pauses definitions with invalid grants
Owner views history (display_status from work items) and controls run/pause/pause-stop/resume/archive

flow:e.title: Event trigger (poll/socket/webhook) > trigger_worker > work
flow:e.summary: Events arrive by webhook ingress (API) or collectors in the event-worker (polls, Slack Socket Mode); each is durably deduped and matched to active trigger revisions in one transaction before acknowledgement; the event-worker admits ready pending runs into ordinary tasks via the shared saved-work path.
